title: Can Deterministic Network Verification Reduce Undetected Faults in LLM‑Generated Configurations?
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (study id c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001) to measure whether inserting a deterministic network verifier between an LLM intent→configuration generator and an emulated execution reduces the proportion of configurations that would execute with operational faults. Using shared_initial_candidate semantics (one identical LLM candidate per intent evaluated both without and with verification), we evaluated 72 preregistered paired intents with gpt-5-mini and a canonical deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution completed with 144 episodes (72 pairs) and 72 model calls. All baseline executions produced no emulator-observed faults (n_11 = 72, n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0). The paired difference in undetected-fault proportion is 0.0 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0], exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap seed = 1729, resamples = 10000). Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate contract this degenerate confirmatory outcome is expected when identical generated candidates produce no baseline execution faults. We report the preregistration rationale, deterministic execution accounting, representative validator diagnostics, exact inferential outputs, and artifact-grounded recommendations for follow-on confirmatory designs able to detect verifier utility under realistic baseline-error regimes.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intents into device-level network configurations. Such automation can accelerate change pipelines but risks silently violating reachability, access-control, ordering, or workflow invariants and thereby causing outages if generated text is executed without additional checks. A common mitigation is a generate–verify–repair (GVR) architecture that pairs stochastic generation with deterministic verification and, when necessary, repair or human review. Despite architectural proposals and prototypes, systematic preregistered paired experiments that isolate verifier detection on identical generated candidates are scarce.

This paper addresses a narrowly scoped, preregistered question: does inserting a deterministic network verifier between an LLM generator and emulator execution materially reduce the proportion of configurations that execute with operational faults when the identical generated candidate is evaluated both without and with verification? We executed preregistered study c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001 with the declared model gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 across 72 paired intents under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The run produced a degenerate confirmatory outcome (no baseline emulator faults), yielding a paired difference of 0.0 (95% CI [0.0,0.0], exact McNemar p = 1.0). We present artifact-grounded analysis explaining this ceiling outcome, clarify design implications for future confirmatory tests, and give concrete preregisterable alternatives that permit measuring verifier utility when baseline error prevalence is non-negligible.
sections.related_work: Prior work shows LLMs can map intent→configuration in constrained vendor‑dialect settings, motivating automation and risk‑mitigation discussion [1]. Multi-agent and tool‑augmented frameworks integrate verifiers or auxiliary services into NetOps workflows, illustrating practical integration points for deterministic checks but typically lack preregistered paired detection evaluations [2]. Generate–verify–repair patterns are well studied in code- and software-repair domains and demonstrate that deterministic validation can materially improve end-to-end correctness when generator error rates are non-negligible and repairs or resampling are permitted [3]. Canonical deterministic network-verification techniques (e.g., header-space analysis and related reachability/policy analyzers) provide precise invariants suitable for the ‘verify’ stage, yet the supplied literature lacks a preregistered paired experiment that measures verifier detection against emulator-executed outcomes on identical candidates [4]. Our study fills that narrow empirical gap under a controlled shared_initial_candidate contract, and its artifacts provide a reproducible template for follow-on designs.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered study c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001 before observing any outcomes. The primary estimand is the paired reduction in undetected operational-fault proportion (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). The hypothesis H1 targeted an absolute paired reduction of 0.20 (two-sided α = 0.05, power ≥ 0.80); preregistered N = 72 pairs (24 per difficulty stratum) followed a sample-size heuristic (preregistration archived).

Shared_initial_candidate contract. The execution_contract enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each intent a single initial LLM generation was produced and that identical candidate was evaluated in two paired conditions. Baseline: execute the shared candidate in an isolated emulator and record emulator-observed faults. Guarded: run the deterministic verifier on the same candidate; if the verifier flags violations the guarded outcome is recorded as prevented (no executed fault); otherwise execute the identical candidate in the emulator. By design any paired difference arises only from the verifier preventing execution of candidates that the emulator would otherwise have failed.

Model and verifier configuration (artifact-grounded). The declared model is gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). Key recorded fields include declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini", provider = "openai_responses", max_output_tokens = 2000, maximum_attempts_per_call = 1, and temperature = null. The recorded temperature = null documents that provider-default runtime sampling semantics were used (this should not be interpreted as an explicit deterministic temperature=0 setting). The canonical verifier used is deterministic_netops_validator_v5 configured with the full_intent_constraint_validation rule set; the verifier emits structured validator_traces per episode (parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration, validation_before/after final_state snapshots, violation_codes, and violation_count). Per-episode verifier traces and scoring artifacts are archived and form the mechanistic basis for guarded decisions.

Task-bank, stratification, and contamination controls. Confirmatory tasks were generated deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Each task manifest encodes a natural-language intent, an ordered required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, initial/expected_final_state snapshots, and difficulty.level (medium/hard/very_hard). Exact-match contamination checks were preregistered and applied; none of the confirmatory pairs were excluded. Confirmatory sampling followed the preregistered stratification (24 pairs per difficulty stratum).

Execution, retries, and deterministic accounting. The missingness_plan allowed up to two retries for transient hosted-API errors. The execution manifest records planned_episode_count = 144, completed_episode_count = 144, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 72. Provider-call audit shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 72 and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 72}, confirming that cross-condition generation activity was limited to a single shared initial generation per pair. Analysis used the registered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor and bootstrap diagnostics (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) as preregistered.

Scoring rule and decision logic. The verifier applied full_intent_constraint_validation that enforces required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and preserve_unspecified_state. Each scoring artifact records a validity verdict and a validator_trace; repair_applied is false in all confirmatory pairs because no verifier flags occurred. All raw responses, scoring JSONs, task manifests, and analysis artifacts are archived for audit.
sections.results:
Execution summary and inferential outcome. The autonomous pipeline completed without technical failures. Key manifest figures: planned_episode_count = 144; completed_episode_count = 144; failed_episode_count = 0; model_calls_used = 72; artifact_count = 510. analysis/condition_summary.csv reports baseline successes = 72, baseline failures = 0 (success_rate = 1.0) and guarded successes = 72, guarded failures = 0 (success_rate = 1.0).

Paired contingency and tests. Aggregating across the 72 confirmatory pairs produced counts n_11 = 72, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 (guarded × baseline). The paired estimate paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) is [0.0, 0.0], reflecting a degenerate distribution due to the absence of discordant pairs. Tabulated artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv) are archived.

Representative per-episode diagnostics. Representative scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json … task-000006-*.json) show validator_traces with parsed_command_count == required_command_count and violation_count = 0. Example extracts: pair-000001 (medium): parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, violation_count = 0. pair-000002 (hard): parsed_command_count = 2, required_command_count = 2, violation_count = 0. These traces confirm the verifier executed on each shared candidate and produced no violation flags across representative tasks.

Contamination and missingness. analysis/contamination_summary.csv reports zero exact-match contaminations. analysis/missingness_summary.csv records complete_pairs = 72 and zero failed or unscorable episodes. Pre-registered sensitivity analyses (treating excluded pairs as failures; bootstrap diagnostics) were executed; because no pairs were excluded and no discordant outcomes occurred, these reproduce the degenerate numeric conclusion.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of the degenerate confirmatory outcome. The preregistered shared_initial_candidate design isolates verifier detection from generator-side resampling or repair, which is a desirable causal property when the goal is to measure detector utility on identical candidates. However, when identical candidates produce zero baseline emulator faults the paired estimand algebraically yields a zero reduction and no discordant pairs can appear. Thus the observed ceiling (paired difference = 0.0; McNemar p = 1.0) is an expected consequence of the design and the data-generating circumstances rather than a statistical or execution error.

Artifact-grounded attribution. Archived artifacts permit concrete attribution of this ceiling: (1) the deterministic task generator encoded explicit required_sequence and allowed_touched_fields that constrained acceptable configurations; (2) the declared model (gpt-5-mini) generated candidates that matched those manifest constraints across the synthetic corpus (shared_initial_candidate SHA entries and response files); (3) the verifier enforced the same constraints (full_intent_constraint_validation) and found no violations (violation_count = 0). These aligned design choices—constrained intents, congruent verifier rules, and model outputs that matched required sequences—explain the absence of baseline emulator faults.

Design implications and preregisterable alternatives. A paired confirmatory test that targets an absolute reduction requires a non-zero baseline prevalence of executed faults to have power. To enable non-degenerate inference under the same infrastructure, we recommend preregistering one or more of the following, each implementable with the archived pipeline: (a) independent-generation arms: permit separate initial generator calls per condition (baseline vs guarded) so the guarded arm can effect resampling or repair-induced distribution shifts; (b) repair-enabled flows: permit a single deterministic repair call when the verifier flags a violation and execute the repaired candidate to measure end-to-end improvement; (c) adversarial/fault-injection task banks: seed tasks with ambiguous wording, ordering subtleties, or vendor-edge cases to raise baseline error prevalence; (d) sampling-parameter sweeps or multi-model comparisons: record explicit non-null temperature and test multiple models to quantify sampling- and model-sensitivity; (e) explicit false-positive cost arms: measure operational blocking cost by comparing blocked-but-safe candidates and associated operational delays. These are methodological changes to the estimand and preregistration but do not rely on new evidence and are supported by the archived execution and analysis infrastructure.
sections.conclusion:
We executed a preregistered paired evaluation (c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001) under shared_initial_candidate semantics to test whether a canonical deterministic verifier reduces the proportion of LLM-generated configurations that would execute with operational faults. For the chosen model (gpt-5-mini), verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and the synthetic/emulated task bank, baseline executions produced zero emulator faults and the verifier did not change outcomes (paired difference = 0.0; bootstrap 95% CI [0.0,0.0]; exact McNemar p = 1.0). This artifact-grounded null/ceiling outcome is internally consistent with the preregistered design: when identical generated candidates produce no executed faults a verifier cannot reduce executed faults under the shared_initial_candidate contract. Measuring verifier utility under realistic error regimes requires preregistered contracts that permit independent or multiple generator samples, repair-enabled flows, adversarial task sets, and multi-model comparisons. The archived artifacts (responses, task manifests, validator traces, execution manifest, and analysis logs) provide a reproducible baseline and a template for those follow-on confirmatory designs and power calculations.

Human role: a Research Director selected the topic family and approved the immutable initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the lock. Models and orchestration: initial generation used gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version recorded in the archived model_configuration) orchestrated via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter; deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = "5.0") served as the canonical verifier; an isolated emulator executed candidate configurations. Preregistration: study c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001 was preregistered and frozen before observing outcomes. Immutable master-prompt reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). The execution and analysis artifacts (model configuration, task manifests, raw responses, per-episode verifier traces, execution manifest, and analysis logs) are archived and available for audit; they are summarized in the paper rather than enumerated here. The archived model_configuration records temperature = null, which indicates provider-default runtime sampling semantics and should not be interpreted as an explicit deterministic temperature setting.
limitations: Confirmatory ceiling/null outcome: the baseline generator produced zero emulator faults on the preregistered task set, preventing direct measurement of verifier detection benefit.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the design measures verifier effect on the same generated candidate only and does not assess independent per-condition generation, multi-sample generation, or repairs unless explicitly permitted by the contract.
Single-model scope: experiments used one declared model (gpt-5-mini); results do not imply generality across models or versions.
Synthetic/emulated tasks: task corpus and emulator executions differ from production devices and live traffic; external validity to production deployments is limited.

Sampling-parameter uncertainty: execution/model_configuration.json shows temperature = null (sampling parameters unset); null indicates provider-default runtime sampling semantics and is a residual uncertainty recorded in the archived configuration.

Residual contamination risk: deterministic provenance and exact-match checks were applied, but private training-data contamination of the hosted model cannot be fully ruled out and remains residual uncertainty.
